item.title: Flattley Pedals Introduces the “Reaper”
item.description:
Sleaford, England – Flattley Pedals has introduced the “Reaper”, the company’s special 10th Anniversary Edition celebratory pedal.


In continuance of Flattley Guitar Pedals 10th anniversary year celebrations, the company has revisited its first ever production pedal “Reaper” created ten years ago but with a twist. The original Reaper product was an overdrive/distortion pedal with a rotary switch that could select variations in the components that were used in the feedback loop of an op amp to give a range of tones.

The Reaper Dual Mode Distortion Anniversary Edition pedal takes a different approach by having both hard and soft clipping around a similar op-amp core but voiced to be more aggressive than the original. The op-amp core is a bit of a nod to rodent related pedals that we have never explored before.

As well as the two clipping modes there is also a boost mode that removes both methods of clipping to give a mode that can push the amplifier preamp into saturation. The company warns that this can get very loud. The gain control has been chosen to be able to force the clean boost to clip as well when approaching maximum.

All of these modes are selected by a three-way toggle switch. This Anniversary Edition features vintage glass envelope germanium diodes for hard clipping, and asymmetric clipping using an LED and conventional silico diode to give a wider range of tones from this versatile pedal. Additional controls set the effect output volume, the overall gain and a tone control that can be used to tame the high end harmonics created by the various clipping modes.


The pedal’s purple halo light rings installed diffuse the light when playing live, so you can avoid being blinded by standard LEDs, and a purple laser etched aluminium foot topper gives you more real estate for contact when switching the pedal on and off during quick changes when playing live.

All Flattley "Platinum Range" pedals are hand processed in Flattley’s paint shop, with a strikingly unique finish.

The Reaper includes this control set:

Toggle Switch:

HC= Hard Clipping

BST=Boost Function

SC= Soft Clipping


Reaper Controls

  • Volume: Controls the overall output level.
  • Gain: Controls the amount of gain/overdrive
  • Tone: Controls the amount of treble/bass

Other features include:

  • 9-volt external power operation (no internal battery option)
  • 20mm black anodised aluminium custom etched control knobs
  • Purple halo light rings installed
  • The Reaper comes with a purple custom etched aluminium foot topper

All Flattley pedals are handmade and hand wired in the UK using the highest quality components.

The Flattley Reaper carries a street price of $319/£259/€319. For more information visit flattleyguitarpedals.com.

item.title: Rig Rundown: The Barbarians of California
item.description:
PG’s Chris Kies met up with the Barbarians of California at the Exit/In in Nashville, one show into a tour behind their second record, Megatons. Eric Stenman, Zach Irons, and Dave Amezcua walked through a setup shaped by fly dates, borrowed backline, and a band with no techs. Have a look at some quick highlights below, and tune into the new Rig Rundown for all the details.

Brought to you by D’Addario.

Good Hammer


Stenman calls the Les Paul the core of most of what he does, going back to seeing pictures of Jimmy Page holding one. This one has Slash pickups in it, and he’s honest about the tradeoff: they don’t stay in tune especially well, but they feel cool. The band lives between drop C and drop B-flat, which used to mean hauling four guitars to cover a main and a backup in each. With no budget and no techs on fly dates, they now keep everything in one tuning and pitch-shift between songs from their floorboards. Stenman’s strings are .012–.054; when he had a dedicated B-flat guitar he ran .014–.056.

Second String


His other guitar is an ESP LTD TED-600T Ted Aguilar signature, which he says plays better than the Les Paul—quicker and easier under the hand. Which one comes out depends on the week.

Valhalla Rising


Valhalla sent three heads out with the band for this run, two guitar and one bass, delivered to their Oklahoma date a few days earlier. Everyone’s still learning them. Stenman does his tone-shaping digitally, but says he still wants an amp onstage so he can feel the air and the tubes.

Double Helix


The Line 6 Helix is the brain of Stenman’s rig. He leans on a Rectifier model, switches to an ENGL setting for certain songs, and piles delay and reverb onto the leads—he traces the washed-out stuff to Britpop and shoegaze.

Whammy Wanted


Irons found this 1985 Carvin V220, Kahler and all, online during a Deftones tour and bought it sight unseen—being left-handed, he rarely gets to try anything first. He wanted a bar for dive bombs and Dimebag squeals, which he’d been approximating on a hardtail and hating. It’s never been set up and it works. The dip switches are coil taps, and the pickups are staying put.

Zach Irons’ Pedalboard


Irons found his Empress Heavy by typing “best heavy metal pedal” into a search bar and buying the first result; it’s the only distortion he’s used in this band, pushed by an MXR Micro Amp. A Boss XS-1 handles the drop tunings, while the wah is a Triangulo Lab WH-X clone of an Ibanez WH-10, sent to him by the Italian builder who makes John Frusciante’s replicas. An EHX Holy Grail covers reverb, and a Moog MF Delay gets used for between-song infinity washes. A Boss TU-2 keeps everything in tune, and a Voodoo Lab Pedal Power 2 Plus assures everything’s running.

Party P


Amezcua’s 1978 Fender Precision is completely unmodified and has been with him through Under the Influence of Giants, AWOLNATION, and now this band. Strings vary depending on who’s giving them away, though usually Ernie Ball.

What’s Left


Amezcua calls his board the one that could have been. A rained-out set at Shiprock took out a delay, an EHX pedal, and an octave, so he’s down to an Aguilar DI for tone and punch, a Strymon Zuma power supply, and a Boss TU-3 tuner — which he needs, since he’s the only one in the band tuning by hand between songs.

item.title: P-90, Filter'Tron, And Specialty Classics | Pickups Demystified Ep. 3
item.description:
The humbucker-versus-single-coil debate has a blind spot. Technically, a P-90 is a single coil and a Filter'Tron is a humbucker, so both get filed away with the usual suspects. Plug one in and you'll hear why that shortcut doesn't hold up.


In the final episode of Pickups Demystified, Tom Butwin digs into the specialty pickups that share a family tree with the two big categories but took their own path. The P-90 uses a wider coil and bar magnets for a grittier midrange than any Strat-style single coil. The Filter'Tron cancels hum like a PAF, but its narrow bobbins and thicker magnet give it a brighter, tighter voice. Tom walks through the history behind each design and highlights modern takes, including a few that drop straight into a humbucker route.

Then come the outliers. The Charlie Christian blade pickup dates back to the 1930s and helped turn the electric guitar into a lead instrument. The wide-range humbucker was Fender's oversized answer to Gibson in the early seventies, designed by Seth Lover, the same engineer behind the PAF. item.title: Seymour Duncan Unveils Duncan Distortion 50th Anniversary Set
item.description:
Seymour Duncan has unveiled the Duncan Distortion Limited Edition 50th Anniversary Custom Shop Set.


Each set is built to exacting standards in the company’s custom shop by a small, elite team led by Maricela “MJ” Juarez. Limited to only 500 sets worldwide, all are built to original specifications and include replica “Seymourized” and model name stickers, just like the earliest builds that collectors have hunted for decades. Lightly aged for vintage character, each set arrives in exclusive 50th Anniversary packaging in your choice of black or zebra, with bottom plates hand-signed by Seymour and MJ.


Key features:

  • Limited 50th Anniversary Custom Shop Set: a one-time run of only 500 sets, honoring one of Seymour Duncan's most aggressive and enduring designs
  • Original high-output ceramic humbucker: large ceramic magnet and hot coil windings deliver tight, percussive lows, searing highs, and a cutting upper midrange
  • True to original specs: built with butyrate bobbins, long-leg baseplates, and maple spacers, while staying faithful to the classic Duncan Distortion voice
  • Paired with the Seymourizer II neck pickup (later renamed Duncan Distortion Neck): fluid sustain under gain, with articulate clean tones
  • Hand-built by the company’s Custom Shop team: includes bottom plates hand-signed by Seymour W. Duncan and MJ
  • Vintage-correct details: lightly aged for authentic character, and includes replica "Seymourized" and model stickers
  • Exclusive 50th Anniversary packaging
  • Available in either choice of black or zebra


The Duncan Distortion bridge pickup is Seymour's original high-output ceramic humbucker. Built with a large ceramic magnet and hot coil windings, it delivers tight, percussive lows, searing highs, and a powerful upper midrange that cuts through any mix. It retains clarity while driving amps harder, giving players the raw, immediate response that defined decades of rock and metal. The sonic formula of this set remains unchanged from the production models, and preserves the classic aggressive voice favored by legends like Randy Rhoads, George Lynch and Adam Jones. Paired with the hot Seymourizer II neck pickup (later renamed Duncan Distortion Neck) as the perfect complement, the set delivers fluid sustain under gain while maintaining articulate clean tones.

The core design of the Duncan Distortion was set when production began in the late '70s, and it hasn't changed since. Over the years, small adjustments were made to improve consistency and player flexibility, like bobbins better suited for vacuum wax potting. This exclusive 50th Anniversary Custom Shop version honors our history by returning to early specs including butyrate bobbins, long-leg baseplates, and maple spacers, while staying true to the classic Duncan Distortion tone.

The Duncan Distortion Limited Edition 50th Anniversary Custom Shop Set carries a street price of $375.00. For more information visit seymourduncan.com.
